stem: Karan borrows Rs 40,000 at 6% per annum compounded annually. He repays Rs 15,000 at the end of Year 1. What is the outstanding balance at the end of Year 2 (after no payment in Year 2)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Mid-loan repayments reset the compounding base; the two-year factor applies only to whatever balance remains after the repayment, not to the original principal.

Rs 31,900 = 40000 x 1.06 x 1.06 - 15000 x 1.06 applies Year 2 growth to the repayment itself as if the repayment also earns interest, wrongly treating the Rs 15,000 as a deposit rather than a payment made at end-Year 1.

Rs 27,614 = 40000 x 1.1236 - 15000 applies the two-year compound factor (1.06)^2 to the original principal and subtracts the repayment at the very end, ignoring that repayment occurred at end of Year 1 and so only the post-repayment balance of 27400 grows in Year 2.

Rs 30,350 = (40000 - 15000) x 1.1236 applies the two-year factor to the original principal net of repayment (25000) as if the repayment were made on Day 0, not end of Year 1; it ignores the interest that accrued on 40000 during Year 1.

explanation: Step 1: End of Year 1 before repayment: 40000 x 1.06 = Rs 42,400. After repayment: 42400 - 15000 = Rs 27,400. Step 2: End of Year 2: 27400 x 1.06 = Rs 29,044.

explanation_sections.punchline: Mid-loan repayments reset the compounding base; the two-year factor applies only to whatever balance remains after the repayment, not to the original principal.
explanation_sections.approach: Step-by-step: (1) Year 1 end balance = 40000 x 1.06 = 42400; subtract repayment 42400 - 15000 = 27400. (2) Year 2 end balance = 27400 x 1.06 = 29044. Two multiplications, one subtraction.
explanation_sections.lesson: Whenever a payment occurs between compounding periods, break the problem into phases. Never apply a multi-year factor to the original principal when interim cash flows exist.
explanation_sections.timing: 90 seconds: two sequential multiplications and one subtraction. Trap is option 3 (two-year factor applied to original P, repayment subtracted at the end).
